questions.explain: $ad - bc = 3 \cdot 2 - 1 \cdot 2 = 4$. Adding the products ($6 + 2 = 8$) is the classic slip.

questions.q: The preset **Mirror world (flip)** is $\begin{pmatrix} 1 & 0.2 \\ 0.6 & -0.4 \end{pmatrix}$ with $\det = -0.52$. What happens to the unit square?
options: It becomes a parallelogram of area 0.52 with flipped orientation
It gets a negative area of −0.52
questions.explain: Area is $|\det| = 0.52$; the negative sign means orientation is reversed (like a mirror), not that area is negative.

questions.q: If you multiply a 2×2 matrix by 3 (both columns tripled), how does the determinant change?
questions.explain: In 2D, $\det(kM) = k^2 \det(M)$: each side of the parallelogram triples, so area scales by $3 \times 3 = 9$.

questions.q: The **Near-singular** preset has $\det = 0.0075$. What does that mean?
options: The plane is almost flattened but still not collapsed — the matrix is still invertible
The plane collapsed to a line exactly
questions.explain: A tiny but non-zero determinant means the parallelogram is very thin. Only $\det = 0$ means a full collapse.
